transitions.historical_text: As long as this card remains face-up on the field, destroy all monsters with an ATK equal to 1400 or less that are Normal Summoned or Special Summoned.
transitions.modern_text: Destroy all monsters with an ATK of 1400 or less that are Normal Summoned or Special Summoned.
transitions.summary: Wording modernisation only: CP01-EN014 drops the 'As long as this card remains face-up on the field' preamble and the 'an ATK equal to' phrasing. The mandatory destruction of every Normal or Special Summoned monster with 1400 or less ATK is unchanged.

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the added 'This card must be face-up on the field to activate and to resolve this effect' clause (BP01-EN129, Battle Pack: Epic Dawn)

transitions.historical_text: Destroy all monsters with an ATK of 1400 or less that are Normal Summoned or Special Summoned.
transitions.modern_text: When a monster(s) with 1400 or less ATK is Normal Summoned or Special Summoned: Destroy those monsters with 1400 or less ATK. This card must be face-up on the field to activate and to resolve this effect.
transitions.summary: Functional erratum: BP01 added 'This card must be face-up on the field to activate and to resolve this effect', which the modern script enforces with the extra clause 'not eg:IsContains(e:GetHandler())' in the condition of its mandatory summon trigger. Under the era text the trigger also fires when King Tiger Wanghu itself is part of the summoned group, so a simultaneous Special Summon of Wanghu together with monsters of 1400 or less ATK destroys those monsters; the modern card does not activate at all in that case. Everything else is identical in both scripts: a mandatory (TRIGGER_F) field trigger on EVENT_SUMMON_SUCCESS and EVENT_SPSUMMON_SUCCESS, filtering face-up monsters with 1400 or less ATK, suppressed while Wanghu is battle-destroyed.

rulings_check.difference: Era: when King Tiger Wanghu is Summoned at the same time as other monsters with 1400 or less ATK (e.g. by one Cyber Jar resolution), its effect triggers and destroys those other monsters; modern: it does not activate at all when it is itself part of the summoned group ('must be face-up on the field to activate'). Era: if Wanghu itself is Summoned with an effective ATK of 1400 or less (because of a pre-existing effect), it destroys itself; modern: it does not activate when it is itself the summoned monster, so it survives.

review.notes:
Chain starts at lineage v1 (DB2-EN207, 2005-07-27), the version the GOAT entry's text matches exactly. The earlier v0 (PGD-004, 2003-07-18) -> v1 transition dropped the '(excluding Flip Summon)' parenthetical; that is a clarification removal rather than a behaviour change (neither script hooks a Flip Summon event - only EVENT_SUMMON_SUCCESS and EVENT_SPSUMMON_SUCCESS), and it predates the baseline, so it is recorded here rather than in changes. Trailing lineage v4 (OP24-EN004, 2024-02-14) rewords to 'If a monster(s) ... is Normal or Special Summoned while you control this card'; the pinned cdb text is still v3, so v4 is not recorded. Upstream annotation on the GOAT script: 'Triggers on its own summon'.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, King Tiger Wanghu). The rulings read support d1, d2 at both snapshots (the passages are in the check); nothing contradicts a claimed difference, so kind, summary and coverage are unchanged. Verdicts: [c1] d1 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu; d2 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu.
